summary.value: An ancestral restoration ground where skeletons maintain monuments and teach younger generations their history — the hero calls it a battlefield. Its resident cast: swarmers skeleton-grunt, bat-cave, and ghost-spectral; chasers skeleton-knight and centipede-bone; shooter skeleton-archer; bomber ghost-pale; sniper skeleton-mage; and turret eyemonster-watcher. The 'waves' are groundskeepers, teachers, and relatives arriving to contain the intruder desecrating their memorials.

sharedOpinions.reason: He smashes memorial lamps and pockets the pieces as 'shards'. We restore what we can and record the rest — the record will outlast him.
The Crypt keeps the names; we keep the ground. Between us, no one is lost twice.
Monument work is heavy work. They have righted more fallen obelisks than any crew of ours, and never cracked one.

examples.value: Stone forgets slowly; that is why we build with it.
Repair is a slower argument than ruin, and it wins.

meaning.value: The restoration commons itself — open to every realm's dead and every realm's mourners. Calling it a 'yard' is affection, not disrespect.
The recently restored, still relearning their histories at the monuments. The hero's 'skeleton army' is, in part, a field trip.

customs.value: Restoration shifts end with a history lesson at whichever monument was repaired that day. Work and remembrance are the same hour.
Memorial lamps are lit at dusk in the order the names are read. No lamp is skipped, whatever the weather or the emergency.

taboos.value: Never lean, climb, or shelter behind a monument in a fight. The groundskeepers will shield the stone with their own bodies — the hero counts this as aggression.
Never pocket a memorial lamp or its pieces. Broken lamps are gathered for repair; taking them is theft from the dead.
